headline_marked: 30 banks face [[digital services disruption]] until Oct 10
headline: 30 banks face digital services disruption until Oct 10
summary: Card, ATM, and digital transactions are hampered for millions of users due to technical maintenance of the Q-Cash network.
details: Digital transactions for customers of at least 30 banks are being disrupted due to the temporary suspension of 'Q-Cash', a network-based payment switch operated by IT Consultants (ITC).
The disruption began on October 4 at 9 PM and is expected to continue until October 10 at 12 PM. The cause is cited as technical upgrades, system migration, and maintenance activities.
Bangladesh Bank has summoned the Q-Cash management authority and issued directives to restore all switching card-related services as soon as possible.

Banks that have their own independent switching systems are still able to process card transactions. However, those without alternative arrangements have seen their ATM and card services completely shut down.

Affected customers are unable to withdraw cash from ATMs, transfer funds, or perform e-commerce and international transactions. Some employees have even reported being unable to withdraw their salaries.
Bangladesh Bank clarified that transactions through the NPSB platform, mobile financial services (MFS), and other payment service providers remain operational and unaffected.

Banks that have their own independent switching systems are still able to process card transactions. However, those without alternative arrangements have seen their ATM and card services completely shut down.

headline_marked: Shoe garland hung on [[Bir Sreshtha Hamidur Rahman sculpture]] in Jhenaidah
headline: Shoe garland hung on Bir Sreshtha Hamidur Rahman sculpture in Jhenaidah
summary: Photos of the desecrated monument of the 1971 war hero went viral on social media, sparking widespread anger among locals.
details: Unknown people hung a garland of shoes on a sculpture of Bir Sreshtha Hamidur Rahman in Jhenaidah. The incident occurred at the central bus terminal area, where the sculpture is currently under construction.

Photos of the desecrated monument spread rapidly on social media on Tuesday morning, causing widespread anger among local residents. The shoes were removed by midday, according to Kamaluzzaman, a leader of the district's Muktijoddha Sangsad.

Jhenaidah Sadar Police chief Md Asaduzzaman stated that police learned of the incident through Facebook and have launched an investigation. District Commissioner Md Noman Hossain has also instructed police to take legal action against those responsible.

Bir Sreshtha Hamidur Rahman was born in Jhenaidah and was posthumously awarded Bangladesh's highest military honour for his sacrifice in the 1971 Liberation War. He was killed on October 28, 1971, in combat against Pakistani forces in Kamalganj, Moulvibazar.
